source.author: hor
source.text: atque ego cum Graecos facerem, natus mare citra, versiculos, vetuit me tali voce Quirinus post mediam noctem visus, cum somnia vera: in silvam non ligna feras insanius ac si magnas Graecorum malis inplere catervas.
source.text_original: atque ego cum Graecos facerem, natus mare citra,  / versiculos, vetuit me tali voce Quirinus  / post mediam noctem visus, cum somnia vera:   / 'in silvam non ligna feras insanius ac si  / magnas Graecorum malis inplere catervas.'
source.text_english: And when I was making little Greek verses, born this side of the sea, Quirinus appeared to me after midnight in a dream, and forbade me with these words—for dreams are true: into the forest you would not carry wood more foolishly than if you were to want to fill the great ranks of the Greeks.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Quod opusculum meum, si in Graecum ut polliceris transtuleris, , et imperitiae meae doctissimos quoque viros testes facere volueris, dicam tibi illud Horatianum: In silvam ne ligna feras.
reuse.text_original: Quod opusculum meum, si in Graecum (ut polliceris) transtuleris, ἀντιφιλονείκων τοῖς κατασύρουσιν, et imperitiae meae doctissimos quoque viros testes facere volueris, dicam tibi illud Horatianum: In silvam ne ligna feras.
reuse.text_english: If you translate this little work of mine into Greek, as you promise, and wish to make even the most learned men witnesses to my lack of skill, I shall say to you that Horatian line: Do not carry wood into the forest.
